text:
customer-jane: Hey team, we've got a Private deployment in our VPC that sits behind a corporate HTTP proxy. Since yesterday outbound requests from the agent to https://api.redwood.com sometimes fail with TLS handshake errors and sometimes succeed but arrive at your side without the Authorization header (causing 401s). Can you help?

support-bot: Thanks for the report — we've flagged this for support. Can you share a minimal repro (curl -v) and any agent logs?

alex: Hi @customer-jane — a couple quick Qs: what proxy product/version is in front of the agent (BlueCoat/ISA/ProxySG/etc)? Is the proxy using explicit CONNECT tunnels for 443 or doing TLS interception (MITM)?

customer-jane: It's our corporate proxy (transparent corporate appliance) that enforces auth. We don't have the vendor name handy. Repro curl attached below. Note: the agent is configured with http_proxy pointing at proxy.corp:8080.

customer-jane: ```
$ curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:8080 -H "Authorization: Bearer BADTOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
* Connected to proxy.corp (10.10.10.5) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT api.redwood.com:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com:443
> Proxy-Authorization: Basic ********
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
< Proxy-agent: corp-proxy/2.1
* Proxy replied OK to CONNECT request
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* server certificate: /C=US/ST=CA/L=SF/O=Corp-Proxy/CN=corp-proxy.local
* SSL: certificate subject: CN=corp-proxy.local
* SSL: certificate verify result: self signed certificate in certificate chain (18), continuing.
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com
> Authorization: Bearer BADTOKEN
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
< Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 12:34:56 GMT
< Content-Type: text/plain
< Connection: close
<
* Closing connection 0
```

customer-jane: When we check our proxy logs the upstream request shows Authorization header missing and Host rewritten to the proxy host. We also see the CONNECT appears to succeed but the TLS server name is corp-proxy.local (proxy's MITM cert). When the agent retries without proxy (from a jump host) it works fine.

maria: Looks like the proxy is doing TLS interception (MITM) and also rewriting headers. Two separate failure modes here: 1) TLS interception without installing the proxy CA into the private agent's trust store => cert mismatch/TLS verify failures; 2) proxy-request rewriting that strips or truncates Authorization or rewrites Host. Both would cause the symptoms you describe (401s, 400s).

eng-oncall-raj: Can you also paste the agent's debug log around the request? I'm looking for whether the agent is using CONNECT/TUNNEL or performing outbound plain HTTP to the proxy with the absolute-URI (which some proxies treat differently).

customer-jane: Agent log snippet: ```
[2026-07-06T12:34:56Z] outbound: proxy=http://proxy.corp:8080 method=CONNECT dest=api.redwood.com:443 result=ok
[2026-07-06T12:34:56Z] tls: server_name=api.redwood.com negotiated=true verified=false verify_error=certificate signed by unknown authority
[2026-07-06T12:34:56Z] request: route=/v1/health headers={Host: api.redwood.com, Authorization: REDACTED} sent_bytes=184
[2026-07-06T12:34:56Z] upstream: response_status=400 headers={Connection: close}
```

infra-ops: Two likely proxy behaviors to check: (A) proxy intercepts TLS and terminates/re-issues certificate (MITM). If the agent doesn't trust the proxy CA the handshake will show verify=false (we see that). (B) some corporate proxies implement an HTTP/1.0 canonicalization or security rule that strips Authorization when they consider the request 'cross-domain' or exceed header length. Also a handful of proxies rewrite Host to the proxy internal name when they serialize logs, which can be confusing.

security: If the proxy is doing TLS interception, is the customer's policy to install the interception CA onto all hosts? If not, the agent must use a tunneled CONNECT and trust the upstream cert. From the curl output you pasted it looks like CONNECT is used but then the proxy still performed MITM (returned its own cert). That indicates it is intercepting CONNECT too (corporate appliances can do that).

alex: Quick repro commands to help isolate (please run from the agent host):
1) Verify SNI and server cert chain bypassing the proxy (if possible):
   curl -v --resolve api.redwood.com:443:34.210.12.34 https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
2) Probe via the proxy and dump raw bytes:
   curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:8080 --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
3) Check whether Authorization is present when proxy receives the CONNECT vs upstream: review proxy access logs for both stages.

maria: Temporary mitigations while you work with infra/security team:
- If policy allows, add api.redwood.com to NO_PROXY for the agent so the proxy is bypassed (best).
- If NO_PROXY is not allowed, require the proxy to allow opaque CONNECT tunnels to api.redwood.com over 443 without terminating them.
- Ensure the proxy isn't performing header stripping for Authorization/Proxy-Authorization. Some proxies have a rule called "RemoveSensitiveHeaders" or similar.

customer-jane: NO_PROXY not allowed by policy. Proxy team says they must authenticate traffic and perform inspection. They can however add an exception to allow CONNECT passthrough to a small set of hostnames/IPs. What IP ranges should we give them?

eng-oncall-raj: We can provide a stable list of Redwood public egress IPs for the hosted API; I'll open a ticket with ops to get the current published IP list. For Private deployments, if you're pointing at api.redwood.com we recommend adding both the DNS names and the IP ranges to an allowlist. I'll follow up with the ops list in this thread.

infra-ops: Also ask proxy team to check for header length limits and any URL/host canonicalization rewrite rules. If the proxy rewrites Host to its internal hostname in the upstream request, that will break SNI and cert validation.

security: Another workaround is to tunnel TCP over an enterprise-approved egress gateway that performs authentication but preserves TLS end-to-end (so the agent sees the real Redwood cert). That keeps inspection and satisfies policy while avoiding header stripping.

customer-jane: OK — I'll gather proxy logs for the CONNECT session and ask them to try an allowlist for api.redwood.com IPs. Also can you escalate for a better error that distinguishes "missing Authorization header upstream" vs "local TLS verify failure"? The agent log message is ambiguous for our SREs.

alex: Filed ENG-12345 to track improving the agent error surface for proxy interception vs header-stripping. Action items: 1) @customer-jane share proxy logs for the failed CONNECT and the upstream request; 2) proxy team test adding an allowlist for api.redwood.com IPs or enabling opaque CONNECT to those hosts; 3) we (eng) will provide the published IP ranges and follow up on the agent error message change.

support-bot: Thanks — tagging infra-ops and security for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

customer-jane: Thanks all — will upload logs once I have them. Appreciate the next steps.
